channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: The Pound sells its own inflation spike ahead of a Fed hike
item.description: The Pound trades just above 1.3450, down 23 pips, after a morning that ran in two directions. It climbed into the August inflation release at 06:00 GMT, spiked on it, then spent six hours handing the move back and another 30 pips with it.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average huddles ahead of Fed action
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades just above 52,100 and has spent the Wednesday morning going nowhere, on the day the Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise its rate for the first time since 2023. That is not indifference.

item.title: Euro: Consolidation with downside risks against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Euro (EUR) is consolidating in a tight range around the mid-1.15s as markets await the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

item.title: US Dollar: Fed repricing risk caps downside – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes the US Dollar (USD) has outperformed G10 peers on expectations the Fed will deliver around 100 bps of tightening over 12 months, but warns this may be excessive.

item.title: British Pound: BoE repricing risk grows – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes GBP/USD is trading heavy near its 200-day moving average as United Kingdom (UK) gilts stabilize. August Consumer Price Index (CPI) slightly exceeded the Bank of England's (BoE) projections, but he still expects the BoE to hold rates at 3.75%.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds ground as Fed decision looms
item.description: AUD/USD trades in a narrow range on Wednesday as investors hold back from taking strong positions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, AUD/USD trades around 0.7134, little changed on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC hawkish tilt and key levels – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/CAD is steady near 1.39 as markets await the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Canada’s (BoC) summary of deliberations. They note the BoC is likely to sound more hawkish after firmer inflation data and still-accommodative policy.

item.title: United Kingdom: BoE hold view reinforced – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Global Markets Research team, including Josie Anderson, George Buckley and Andrzej Szczepaniak, notes that UK CPI data for August came in broadly as expected, with headline inflation at 3.1% and core and services measures unchanged.

item.title: Gold consolidates gains as traders brace for Fed interest rate decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates gains on Wednesday after advancing during Asian trading hours, supported by a modest pullback in Oil prices and US Treasury yields. The move helps the precious metal recover from its lowest level in over a month, touched earlier this week.

item.title: Federal Reserve set to raise interest rate after five meetings on hold
item.description: The United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) announces its interest rate decision on Wednesday, following another pivotal meeting that could provide key insights into the monetary policy outlook heading into the end of the year.

item.title: Eurozone: Manufacturing outlook steadies as year-end hopes build – ING
item.description: ING’s Bert Colijn notes that Eurozone industrial production slipped by 0.1% in both June and July, leaving output broadly unchanged from a year earlier. He highlights resilience in capital goods and energy, but continued weakness in consumer-focused sectors, especially non-durable goods.

item.title: Euro trades cautiously against US Dollar ahead of expected Fed rate hike
item.description: EUR/USD consolidates losses on Wednesday as traders avoid taking strong directional positions ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Silver price rebounds ahead of expected Fed rate hike, Warsh press conference
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds on Wednesday and trades around $64.00 per troy ounce at the time of writing, up 1.32% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed pricing creates asymmetric risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad says the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by energy-driven risk aversion ahead of the FOMC decision.

item.title: Bank of England: Hawkish hold risks and November hike – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Henry Cook expects the Bank of England to deliver a hawkish hold, with UK inflation driven higher by energy and headline CPI projected to exceed 4% after the January price cap reset.

item.title: Euro: Markets test ECB reaction function – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen notes that EUR money markets now discount more than four additional European Central Bank (ECB) rate hikes beyond the two already delivered, as investors push expectations ahead of policymakers.

item.title: United States Retail Sales rose by 1.2% MoM in August
item.description: Retail Sales in the United States increased to $773.9 billion in August, the US Census Bureau reported on Wednesday. This print represents a monthly gain of 1.2%, a reversal of the 0.5% contraction recorded in the previous month, and came in above market expectations (+0.8%).

item.title: British Pound: Sterling stability challenged by narrowing carry – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Shreyas Gopal notes that Bank of England (BoE) meetings have repeatedly seen early market speculation on tightening fade as decisions approach, keeping the Pound stable and EUR/GBP in a narrow range.

item.title: US Dollar: Modestly bearish path under gridlock – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Jayati Bharadwaj expects a divided Congress to keep macro fundamentals as the main driver for FX, maintaining a modestly bearish view on the Dollar into year-end.

item.title: British Pound extends losses against Euro with BoE decision in focus
item.description: EUR/GBP extends its recovery on Wednesday after bouncing from the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at 0.8555 on Monday, its lowest level in two weeks.

item.title: Euro: Recovery does not justify stronger EUR – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that while Eurozone growth and inflation risks are real, being long the Euro (EUR) is not the best way to express this view.

item.title: British Pound: Data back Bank of England pause – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen highlights that United Kingdom (UK) inflation matched expectations at 3.1% y/y, with higher energy and fuel prices driving the rise, while core and services Consumer Price Index (CPI) remained unchanged.

item.title: Canadian Dollar tests monthly lows against US Dollar ahead of Fed decision
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades lower against a firm US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the market positioned for a quarter rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed), the first one in three years, later in the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds its ground ahead of highly anticipated Fed decision
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7130 on Wednesday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day, as investors remain cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed path and credibility in focus – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke notes that the FOMC is widely expected to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points after stronger-than-expected August inflation. She argues that a surprise pause would hurt Fed credibility and the Dollar, while a hike is largely priced in.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains close to seven-week low on Wednesday, Fed's policy in focus
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) holds onto over-a-week long losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Growth risks temper RBNZ pricing – ING
item.description: ING notes that New Zealand’s Q2 GDP slowdown could magnify market impact given infrequent data, but the Reserve Bank of New Zealand remains focused on inflation and jobs.

item.title: Euro trades with caution against US Dollar ahead of Fed’s policy meeting
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades subduedly at around 1.1535 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The major currency pair trades cautiously ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement at 18:00 GMT.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Downside risk persists against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD has pulled back after Monday’s sharper-than-expected drop, with intraday price action now seen confined to a 0.7100–0.7140 band.

item.title: Why is the US Dollar firm when the Federal Reserve hike is already fully priced in?
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is trading with a firm undertone heading into the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) interest rate decision, supported by a relentless march higher in US Treasury yields that has pushed the 10-year yield to 5.00% and the 2-year yield to 4.66%.
